notes: Parent uses subagent_spawn to launch one general-purpose subagent, then explicitly blocks on subagent_wait/subagent_read_result before replying (the recipe prompt names both tools to force the blocking shape and avoid silently degenerating into 3.2 background-subagent's fire-and-forget shape -- the corpus's own dominant pattern is 30 subagent_spawn calls vs only 9 subagent_wait calls system-wide, so this is NOT the model's default). parent_session_birth/parent_turn_start follow the same single-birth FilesUnderRoot pattern as 2-1 basic-turn. child_session_birth+parent_linked assert the generic, path-based ParentSessionIDFromPath linkage (adapter.go:173-191) that fires for ANY <parent>/subagent/<child>/ directory. CONTAMINATION WARNING (see metadata.json caveats): muse fires ambient skill-reminder/goal-reminder/verify-reminder micro-agents on nearly every turn, and any reminder that emits output ALSO gets its own ParentSessionID-linked subagent/ directory (format-spec sec9(b)) -- structurally indistinguishable from a real subagent at the generic daemon-event level. This exact class already produced a vacuous pass on the sibling cell 4-1 multiple-sessions-same-cwd. child_session_birth therefore carries min_delay_ms to skip past a same-turn reminder's own near-instant linkage, and record must additionally cross-check the raw parent transcript's task_stream_linked record for the matched child: task_kind:workflow.agent.native with NO display.role:reminder tag identifies the real target (reminders always carry display.role:reminder; the intended subagent carries no display field at all) -- a bare new_session/parent_linked match is not sufficient proof here. intermediate_working's duration_at_least_ms guards against a false-positive reminder match too: a reminder's own working-to-ready arc resolves in a few seconds, while the demo subagent (spawn + explicit blocking wait, dispatched via a real model round-trip) realistically takes longer. parent_turn_end asserts the working->ready transition fires only once the subagent_wait/subagent_read_result tool_batch.effect has closed (bounded well under the tool's own observed 300000ms hard timeout for this trivial one-file-read task).

text: Parent session appears in ready shortly after the muse TUI finishes launching (single-birth FilesUnderRoot, no presession split -- 2-1 basic-turn precedent)
User prompt (run started) drives parent ready -> working

The dispatched subagent's own session.jsonl materializes under <parent>/subagent/<child-id>/ -- min_delay_ms skips past the earliest same-turn ambient reminder child (which would otherwise also satisfy a bare transcript_new search)

Detector emits parent_linked binding child.session_id -> parent.session_id via parentSessionIDFromPath's path-derived linkage (adapter.go:173-191); record must confirm via the raw transcript that this child's task_stream_linked entry carries task_kind:workflow.agent.native with no display.role:reminder tag, not an ambient reminder child

invariants: no state_transition to ready for parent
no state_transition to waiting for parent
text: Parent stays working while the subagent is alive -- the parent's own run does not reach terminal while its subagent_wait/subagent_read_result tool_batch.effect is still open (session_detector_subagent.go hasActiveChildren/holdIfChildrenActive, agent-agnostic); duration_at_least_ms disfavors a false-positive match on a fast-resolving reminder child

Once the subagent reports its result (subagent.control.result_ready / subagent_read_result returns status:ready) the parent's run reaches its own terminal:completed -> turn_done, and with no other live children the session goes working -> ready
